card.name: Fraction and formula dividers in dosing text
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small words that sit where a division or ratio is about to appear, such as the end of a formula term before a dash line and 72, or 'in' and 'per' in 'one in five' or 'one case per million'.

modes.label: Creatinine clearance formula
modes.description: The closing parenthesis, units or dash line in the Cockcroft-Gault formula, just before the divisor.
modes.example: CLcr= [140-age (years)] x weight (kg) (x 0.85 for female patients<<)>> —————————————— 72 x

modes.label: Rate and ratio wording
modes.description: The word 'per' or 'in' that sets up a ratio, as in risk statements or infusion rate formulas.
modes.example: The attributable risk of liver cancers in CHC users is less than one case<< per>> million users.

card.writes: It suppresses closing-bracket-and-slash tokens, so it seems to steer away from a division sign right after.
card.plain: It fires where a formula or ratio is about to be divided or expressed as 'one in five' or 'per million'.
